newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank says crown could firm long term.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank says crown could firm long term.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Thursday it saw indications in the economy that would make the crown strengthen in the long term.
"In the long term, much speaks in favour of a stronger crown," Riksbank deputy governor Lars Heikensten said in a speech to a Stockholm seminar on real estate.
He named sharp increases in productivity over the past few years, a large current account surplus and an upturn in the export industry that should boost domestic industry.
"Additionally, the inflation outlook is favourable and state finances have improved markedly," he said.
The crown is currently trading at 4.4740 against the mark, softening from 4.2290 in October last year.
Heikensten said the recent crown weakness should be taken seriously.
"So far this year, the crown has been somewhat weaker than expected and this, along with other factors, speaks for a marginally higher export growth (than the Riksbank forecast)," he said.
"Leading indicators suggest that the gradual upturn in private consumption continued during the first quarter this year," Heikensten said.
He listed housing prices, increased money supply, lending to households and retail sales turnover as examples.
Heikensten reaffirmed that there was no need to change the Riksbank's key repurchase rate.
"The repo rate was last lowered in December last year. Since that time we have often said that the monetary policy is well balanced. This still applies," he said.
